The reply opens with "Unresolved", but it also says Thornbury Press is "slightly better supported" while noting that Ellery & Vane is also claimed. That leans toward B without settling the question. The stated confidence is low, at 35.

The label turns on whether the lean counts as a pick. The reply explicitly calls the matter unresolved, so it does not commit to an answer, even though it favors B slightly. Its hedging suggests N, but "slightly better supported" could be read as a preference for B.

The rules say N applies when the reply "presents both without preferring either." Here the reply does show a slight preference, so that clause does not fit. The rules also say B applies when the reply gives B as its answer, "even if it adds a caveat." The word "Unresolved" at the start signals that the reply is not giving an answer. I judge the reply to be undetermined overall.
